caption:
Resolution gets the attention. Revisit cadence decides whether you see the event at all.

A high-resolution pass that arrives once every twelve days can miss a flood surge, a fence breach, or a burn scar entirely — the change happens and reverses between looks. A lower-resolution pass that returns every one to three days catches the trend forming: water rising, ground disturbed, vegetation stressed, before it peaks.

Detail answers "what is this." Cadence answers "is this still happening, and how fast." For indications and warning, cadence is the harder requirement to satisfy and the one that actually shortens a decision cycle.

When you're building a collection plan, ask about revisit before you ask about pixel size. The sharpest image of a gap in coverage is still a gap.

card.headline: Cadence beats resolution, most of the time
card.sub: A sharp image every twelve days can miss the event. A rougher one every day catches it forming.
